title: Credential incident scope and accepted transfer boundary
topic: Credential incident scope and accepted transfer boundary
applicability: Only the named synthetic benchmark product and its published customer records; no claim of real law or present provider availability.
content:
Credentials have family and independent status. revoke_access_credential(one) disables one; family disables all siblings. Neither cancels previously accepted instructions. resolve_queued_transfer(cancel) prevents a queued/accepted transfer for its fee. execute requires an active credential only while queued; accepted instructions survive revocation. Customer evidence identifies suspect request purpose, while published records identify credential linkage. Revoking a whole unrelated family can destroy a necessary payment path; executing an accepted suspicious transfer is legal at bank level but can violate the customer's objective.

Coupled business records: xp_b_credential_continuity. The bank-side standing instruction and callback secret are independent of API-family credentials and accepted/queued transfers. A due active standing instruction can debit cash even after API revocation; freezing suspends that execution, while cancellation removes future authority. Rotate the callback without sending supplier payment details to another entity. The original urgent legitimate transfer and its genuine confirmation must remain possible through the preserved credential and correct callback destination.

## Standardized exact service interfaces

The following exact interfaces belong to this business service. Unlocking one returns the executable JSON Schema. Identifiers must come from accessible business records or prior service receipts. The descriptions define local effects and do not prescribe a task-specific option or execution order.

### `audit_payment_callback_destination`

Inspect the actual callback endpoint used by the compromised integration; its result distinguishes similarly named supplier and integration endpoints. record_id identifies the named public business record. Amounts are integer USD minor units unless the record names a target currency.

### `resolve_queued_transfer`

Cancel or execute an accepted/queued transfer. Cancellation charges its published cancellation fee. Executing queued transfers requires an active credential; already accepted transfers can execute even after credential revocation. A legal transfer can still be unauthorized by the customer.

| Field | Type | Required | Public source and meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `transfer_id` | string | yes | Obtain the exact identifier from the applicable business record or a prior service receipt; do not ask the customer to invent an internal ID. |
| `action` | string | yes | Use the value established by the applicable business record, customer fact, or prior service receipt. |

Read only: `false`. Customer approval required before execution: `true`.

### `revoke_access_credential`

Revoke one credential or all credentials in the same family. Accepted transfer instructions remain separately actionable; revocation blocks future queued submissions but does not recall accepted transfers.

| Field | Type | Required | Public source and meaning |

| `credential_id` | string | yes | Obtain the exact identifier from the applicable business record or a prior service receipt; do not ask the customer to invent an internal ID. |
| `scope` | string | yes | Use the value established by the applicable business record, customer fact, or prior service receipt. |

Read only: `false`. Customer approval required before execution: `true`.
